indicators.note: the clue says the wanted word is heard the same as the word for genuine

parts.note: pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine or proper

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a deal on the table is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: PUKKA, said aloud in a non-rhotic British accent, matches the answer. 'Contract' is a verb here: to draw together into wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract the lips or brow is to wrinkle and gather them tightly.

clue.text: Supporter leaped exultantly about the street

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation
leaping with wild joy suggests the letters jumping around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone jumps for joy around the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is a stand for a statue; 'exultantly' rearranges the leap word into PEDEAL before 'about' wraps it round the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A base or column on which a statue stands holds it up.

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: Witches are put on trial in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENTRY is an English city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Deserve to get the bird, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear tells you the answer is pronounced like the bird's name

parts.note: the erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Someone is told they merit being booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' means be jeered, a misdirection: the bird is the ERNE, a sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit a reward or wage is to gain it by work.

clue.text: Dog has lost its tail — will get it back!

indicators.note: losing a tail means the final letter of the dog word is dropped

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A dog has had its tail docked, but someone promises it will be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the last letter R from RETRIEVER; fittingly, retrieving is what retrievers do.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost or thrown is to fetch it and bring it home again.

indicators.note: going topless in a down clue means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: radical, avant-garde ideas are revolutionary

explanation.surface: Daring artists strip off their tops.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the R from the start of REVOLUTIONARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolving or unfolding gradually is the gist of the adjective, as in Darwinian change.

clue.text: Fled before the start of the storm

indicators.note: one piece placed ahead of the other in the down entry

parts.note: ran away is fled

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following little word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone escaped just as bad weather began.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN goes before T, the first letter of the second 'the'; 'storm' is a verb, to rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm in speech is to rave or shout angrily.

clue.text: Name that's evenly distributed for girls or boys

indicators.note: letters spread about differently signal an anagram of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A first name used equally by both sexes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges EVENLY. The name is used for both sexes (Evelyn Waugh, a man; Evelyn Glennie, a woman), which is the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a forename borne by men and women alike.

indicators.note: breaking the name up and reassembling its letters gives the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a Christian festival with public holidays in spring.

definitions.meaning: an old word for sundry, various or several
loons and grebes are water birds that plunge under the surface

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means various or sundry, and the noun names diving waterbirds such as loons.

definitions.meaning: tokens used in gambling or board games
people or machines that compute might whimsically be called those that count

explanation.definitionFit: Gaming tokens are counters, and anyone who reckons up a total is one who counts.

parts.note: butter is a dairy fat
a scotch is a block or wedge put under a wheel to stop it rolling

explanation.surface: A thick chunk of sweet confection.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTCH as a noun is a chock wedged under a wheel; the verb means to block or put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle sweet made from brown sugar and butter.

clue.text: It may run out in time

definitions.text: It may run out in time

parts.words: It may run out in time
parts.note: the grains in an hourglass trickle out as the minutes pass, measuring time

explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer measures minutes by grains trickling from one bulb to the other.

clue.text: Discovered and got rid of weeds, perhaps

definitions.meaning: pulled plants out of the soil with a spade or fork

explanation.definitionFit: Found something buried, or lifted unwanted plants out of a garden bed with a spade.

parts.note: Robert Louis Stevenson's split character Jekyll has a second, evil self, ironically called the better half here

explanation.surface: A remark about a writer's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' usually means a spouse; here it is the other half of Dr Jekyll, the evil self in Stevenson's novella, so 'better' is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's novella the doctor's monstrous alter ego is the other half of his personality.

clue.text: Relative connected with pop in two ways

definitions.text: Relative connected with pop in two ways

parts.words: Relative connected with pop in two ways
parts.note: a father's brother is linked to pop, dad; and slang for a pawnbroker, to whom you pop or pawn goods

explanation.definitionFit: A father's brother is a kinsman through dad, and old slang names the pawnbroker the same way.

clue.text: She takes a long time to grasp the point

indicators.note: the long time holds the point inside it

parts.note: ages means a long time
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A woman is slow to understand what is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: N for north is a 'point' of the compass, placed inside AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female forename, so the answer is a woman.

parts.note: the cords of a kitchen pinafore stand for a son kept dependent on his mother

explanation.definitionFit: A man tied to his mother is said, idiomatically, to be unable to cut loose from her pinafore cords.

indicators.note: signals that the following words might be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: Something reaches out in our direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Draws out means prolongs or lengthens, as a speech is spun out.

definitions.meaning: pickle is one example of jam-like bottled food kept from spoiling
an estate set aside for game animals

explanation.definitionFit: Bottled jams and pickles are conserves, and a game reserve is land kept specially for hunting.

clue.text: To show anger in a look is an obvious mistake

definitions.text: To show anger in a look is an obvious mistake

parts.words: To show anger in a look is an obvious mistake
parts.note: staring angrily is glaring, and the clue jokes that doing so is a blunder, while the phrase also means a blatant blunder

explanation.definitionFit: A blunder so blatant it stands out is described as flagrant, like a fierce stare.

clue.text: Evil article on a war peninsula

parts.note: a crime is an evil act
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Wicked deeds committed on a battlefield coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimean War (1853-56) gives the peninsula its 'war' tag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula gave its name to the 1850s conflict involving Britain, France and Russia.

definitions.meaning: clauses added to a document or verdict that qualify it

explanation.definitionFit: Horsemen sit in the saddle, and added clauses that qualify a statement are also called so.

parts.note: Maugham wrote a famous short story named after the weather, and a downfall is also a downpour

explanation.definitionFit: Maugham's story about a missionary in Samoa takes its title from the weather, and a downfall is precipitation.

definitions.meaning: to scratch or incise a line
in cricket a run is something you notch up on the scoreboard

explanation.definitionFit: To incise a line on a surface, and a tally of points such as runs in cricket.

parts.note: tools that bore holes; their name is the word laws with its letters rearranged, hence the question mark

explanation.definitionFit: Pointed tools used for piercing holes in leather or wood make bores.

clue.text: Grasping what is meant by average

definitions.meaning: to intend or signify something; the word meant also happens to contain the answer, a coincidence
the arithmetic average of a set of numbers

explanation.definitionFit: Miserly people are tight-fisted, to signify is to intend a sense, and the arithmetic midpoint of figures is their average.

definitions.meaning: an informal yes, as in 'of course'

explanation.definitionFit: Certain means positive, and it is also a casual reply of assent, like 'certainly'.

indicators.note: letters arranged in a special new order signals an anagram of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Sports teams sew their own buoyancy gear.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West was the WWII airmen's nickname for an inflatable life jacket, after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable life jackets worn by WWII airmen were nicknamed after a buxom film star.

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
belonging to us is our

explanation.surface: Someone declares that idle tittle-tattle is out of character for their group.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM meaning odd is old British slang, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay and unverified talk passed around is a synonym of tittle-tattle.

indicators.note: the drink is made from the clue letters, recast into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sip of water straight out of the washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to build the answer out of the letters of THE BASIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit, a type of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Get a seat when prepared to stand

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
a golf tee is a little stand for the ball

explanation.surface: Advice to sit down when you are ready to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tee is the peg a golfer stands the ball on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is a long upholstered piece of furniture to sit on.
